intro.text: A number sign (#) is used with this entry because of evidence that Knobloch syndrome-2 (KNO2) is caused by heterozygous mutation in the PAK2 gene (605022) on chromosome 3q29.

checks.claim: Knobloch syndrome-2 (KNO2) is caused by heterozygous mutation in the PAK2 gene.
checks.evidence_quote: We conclude that the KNO2 syndrome in the studied family is dominant and caused by a deleterious variant in the PAK2 gene.
checks.explanation: The abstract describes the variant as monoallelic (heterozygous) and the disorder as dominant.

checks.claim: The PAK2 gene is located on chromosome 3q29.
checks.evidence_quote: Dominant monoallelic variant in the PAK2 gene causes Knobloch syndrome type 2.
checks.explanation: The abstract does not give the chromosomal location, but adding a gene's standard locus (3q29) counts as nomenclature restatement.

paragraphs.text: Knobloch syndrome is a developmental disorder whose main features are eye abnormalities and an occipital skull defect. The eye findings include high myopia, vitreoretinal degeneration and retinal detachment. The skull defect ranges from occipital encephalocele to a milder scalp or bony defect. Knobloch syndrome-2 is the autosomal dominant form associated with PAK2.

checks.claim: Knobloch syndrome is a developmental disorder whose main features are eye abnormalities and an occipital skull defect.
checks.evidence_quote: Knobloch syndrome (KNO) is an autosomal recessive disorder characterized by high myopia, vitreoretinal degeneration with retinal detachment, and congenital encephalocele.
checks.explanation: The abstract describes eye abnormalities and congenital encephalocele. It does not say the defect is occipital, and it does not call the condition a developmental disorder.

checks.claim: The eye findings in Knobloch syndrome include high myopia.
checks.evidence_quote: Knobloch syndrome (KNO) is an autosomal recessive disorder characterized by high myopia

checks.claim: The eye findings in Knobloch syndrome include vitreoretinal degeneration.
checks.evidence_quote: characterized by high myopia, vitreoretinal degeneration with retinal detachment

checks.claim: The eye findings in Knobloch syndrome include retinal detachment.
checks.evidence_quote: characterized by high myopia, vitreoretinal degeneration with retinal detachment

checks.claim: The occipital skull defect in Knobloch syndrome ranges from occipital encephalocele to a milder scalp or bony defect.
checks.evidence_quote: occipital encephalocoele or scalp lesion. ... One case presents with very early onset of severe eye disease, whereas the other is notable for the very mild scalp defect.
checks.explanation: The abstract supports a range from occipital encephalocele to a very mild scalp defect. It does not mention a bony defect.

checks.claim: Knobloch syndrome-2 is the autosomal dominant form of Knobloch syndrome and is associated with PAK2.
checks.evidence_quote: We conclude that the KNO2 syndrome in the studied family is dominant and caused by a deleterious variant in the PAK2 gene.
checks.explanation: The abstract calls KNO2 dominant and caused by PAK2, in contrast to the recessive COL18A1 form.

paragraphs.text: In the family reported by Antonell et al. (2016), Knobloch syndrome was passed down as an autosomal dominant trait with a heterozygous PAK2 mutation.

checks.claim: In the family with Knobloch syndrome reported by Antonell et al. (2016), the disorder was inherited as an autosomal dominant trait.
checks.evidence_quote: We conclude that the KNO2 syndrome in the studied family is dominant
checks.explanation: The content matches this paper. However, the paper is Antonarakis et al. (2021), not 'Antonell et al. (2016)', and the variant was apparently de novo in both siblings, likely from parental germline mosaicism. It was not passed down from an affected parent.

checks.claim: In the family with Knobloch syndrome reported by Antonell et al. (2016), the disorder was associated with a heterozygous PAK2 mutation.
checks.evidence_quote: The variant was monoallelic and apparently de novo in both siblings indicating a likely germ-line mosaicism in one of the parents
checks.explanation: The heterozygous (monoallelic) PAK2 variant is supported, but the draft attributes it to 'Antonell et al. (2016)' when the paper is Antonarakis et al. (2021).

paragraphs.text: Knobloch syndrome-1 (KNO1) is an autosomal recessive form caused by mutation in the COL18A1 gene.

checks.claim: Knobloch syndrome-1 (KNO1) is an autosomal recessive form of Knobloch syndrome.
checks.evidence_quote: Knobloch syndrome (KNO) is an autosomal recessive disorder
checks.explanation: The abstract calls Knobloch syndrome autosomal recessive and links that form to COL18A1. It names the second locus KNO2, which implies the COL18A1 form is KNO1.

checks.claim: Knobloch syndrome-1 (KNO1) is caused by mutation in the COL18A1 gene.
checks.evidence_quote: Analysis of two unrelated KNO families from Hungary and New Zealand allowed us to confirm the involvement of COL18A1 in the pathogenesis of KNO
checks.explanation: The abstract confirms that COL18A1 mutations cause Knobloch syndrome and reports new COL18A1 mutations in the Hungarian family.

paragraphs.text: Antonell et al. (2016) studied a family with Knobloch syndrome in which no COL18A1 mutation was found. Using exome sequencing, they found a heterozygous missense mutation in the PAK2 gene that segregated with the disorder. They presented functional evidence that the mutation impaired PAK2 kinase activity.

checks.claim: Antonell et al. (2016) studied a family with Knobloch syndrome in which no COL18A1 mutation was found.
checks.evidence_quote: there are patients clinically diagnosed as Knobloch syndrome with unknown molecular etiology not linked to COL18A1. We studied an historical pedigree (published in 1998) designated as KNO2
checks.explanation: The abstract implies the family was not linked to COL18A1 but does not say outright that no COL18A1 mutation was found. The citation should also be Antonarakis et al. (2021), not Antonell et al. (2016).

checks.claim: Antonell et al. (2016) used exome sequencing to find a heterozygous missense mutation in the PAK2 gene in a family with Knobloch syndrome.
checks.evidence_quote: Whole exome sequencing of the two affected siblings and the normal parents resulted in the identification of a PAK2 non-synonymous substitution p.(Glu435Lys) as a causative variant. The variant was monoallelic
checks.explanation: The content is supported (exome sequencing, monoallelic missense variant), but the attribution to 'Antonell et al. (2016)' does not match this paper (Antonarakis et al., 2021).

checks.claim: The heterozygous PAK2 missense mutation segregated with Knobloch syndrome in the family studied by Antonell et al. (2016).
checks.evidence_quote: Whole exome sequencing of the two affected siblings and the normal parents resulted in the identification of a PAK2 non-synonymous substitution p.(Glu435Lys) as a causative variant. The variant was monoallelic and apparently de novo in both siblings
checks.explanation: The variant was found in both affected siblings and not in the unaffected parents (apparently de novo), which fits segregation. The abstract does not use the word 'segregated', and the author and year in the citation are wrong.

checks.claim: Antonell et al. (2016) presented functional evidence that the PAK2 missense mutation found in a Knobloch syndrome family impaired PAK2 kinase activity.
checks.evidence_quote: Functional analysis of the p.(Glu435Lys) PAK2 variant in transfected HEK293T cells results in a partial loss of the kinase activity.
checks.explanation: The functional evidence of impaired (partially lost) kinase activity is supported, but the citation should be Antonarakis et al. (2021), not Antonell et al. (2016).

clinical_synopsis.feature: Occipital encephalocele or occipital skull defect
